boundary_note: Bounded first pass for both frozen records in Forrest's Expedition into West Tennessee. Preserve per-engagement dates: Jackson December 19 and Parker's Cross Roads December 31, 1862. Lexington, Trenton, Humboldt and other actions of the expedition are not added. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force text gives two Union brigades of approx. 3,000 (structured US bounds 3,000/3,000) and a Confederate expeditionary brigade; the live field reads 3000 total (US 3000; CS 0;). Jordan and Pryor say the Confederates on the field never exceeded 1,200 with six guns against Dunham's brigade of not less than 1,800, quote Dunham's report as 1,554 and a newspaper as 1,824, and say two fresh brigades later arrived.
claims.rationale: Brigade, army and reported figures differ in scope and timing; the second Union brigade arrived during the action. None is adopted as matched opening strength.

claims.value: Jordan and Pryor say Napier charged without Forrest's orders and was mortally wounded, and that Forrest answered a Federal surrender demand by claiming he had already surrendered before galloping off; NPS says Dunham refused Forrest's demand for unconditional surrender. The live heading ranks Forrest Major General against the frozen Brigadier General.
claims.rationale: Subordinate and army command roles from a commander-endorsed history and a summary; no listed commander receives automatic sole credit. The heading rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen result is Confederate victory, as is the live field. NPS says both sides claimed victory, the Confederate claims appearing more credible, and that the Confederates withdrew across the Tennessee; Jordan and Pryor say Forrest withdrew to Lexington that evening.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Both sides claimed victory; the frozen label is retained.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text and live field agree: 737 total (US 237; CS 500). Jordan and Pryor give Confederate losses of some twenty-five killed, not over seventy-five wounded and about 250 captured, and Federal losses of at least fifty killed, 150 wounded and about 100 prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The commander-endorsed figures differ from the frozen split and are not adopted.

open_questions: Dunham's, Fuller's, Sullivan's and Forrest's reports, returns and casualty reconciliation remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family; Jordan and Pryor is one retrospective Confederate history written from Forrest's papers and notes, for most of whose statements Forrest's prefatory note accepts responsibility. It is not independent of the listed Confederate commander. Reports and newspapers quoted inside it are not additional families.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
